verdict.rationale: Weave's tracing docs say functions are instrumented with `@weave.op()` in Python or wrapped with `weave.op()` in TypeScript, so both languages are covered by first-party SDKs. The GitHub repo corroborates the `weave.op` tracing approach, but the JS/TS side rests on a single docs line. missing for 10: details on the TS SDK's install, package name and feature parity with Python; independent or hands-on corroboration of JS/TS instrumentation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can instrument apps in both Python and JS/TS with officially supported SDKs

citations.quote: When you decorate a function with `@weave.op()` (Python) or wrap it with `weave.op()` (TypeScript), Weave automatically captures its code, inputs, outputs, and execution metadata.
Manually instrument your application’s LLM calls and arbitrary functions to trace, version, and collect feedback about your application
